subject: gov.policy
name: National artificial intelligence strategy
milestone: A readiness assessment delivered to the ministry names its absence
position_end: Not published; the assessment identifies the absence of a specific instrument as the central gap and is to serve as the base for policy
note: no adoption date, drafting body or timetable on record

subject: gov.policy
name: National cybersecurity council
milestone: Created by decree published 2025-12-03
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Created as a consultative body chaired by the President; no source records it convening and no membership list is on file

subject: gov.policy
name: National cybersecurity strategy
milestone: Published in the official gazette 2025-12-03
position_start: None published
position_end: In force, approved in Council of Ministers in October 2025 and signed in November, with six strategic objectives and a two-phase legislative reform whose first phase is the bill

subject: gov.legislate
name: Artificial intelligence bill
milestone: Draft published for public consultation September 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: An 86-article draft in nine chapters out for public consultation, with a single critical-AI category carrying registration, security-risk assessment and emergency-response duties rather than a tiered risk pyramid, extraterritorial reach over activity abroad affecting Angolan interests, a right to explanation and to refuse AI-based decisions, criminal and strict civil liability, and no repeal of existing legislation; no tabling, committee stage or vote on record
sources: 2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial|2025-12-29 Review of Angola's Proposed Law on Artificial Intelligence
note: the draft text is now held; it defers military AI to a separate instrument and excludes scientific research and purely personal use

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybersecurity bill
milestone: Adopted in plenary 2026-08-12 by 104 votes to 56
position_start: No cybersecurity law in force beyond Lei n.º 7/17, and a bill only cleared by the Council of Ministers on 27 October 2025 for transmission to the National Assembly, as part of a package also carrying the bill against false information and draft decrees creating a national cybersecurity centre and council
position_end: Adopted by the National Assembly on 2026-08-12 by 104 votes to 56, on a presidential initiative, with the MPLA for and UNITA against and no abstentions; graduated administrative fines set as multiples of the national minimum wage, from 7 to 70 for individuals on minor infractions up to 500 for individuals and 4,000 for legal persons on the most serious ones; no promulgation, gazette number or entry into force on file. It requires telecommunications operators to transmit any communication whose content is criminal or prejudicial to state security, which UNITA and part of civil society object to as leaving unclear which content qualifies and on what terms subscribers' personal data reaches the authorities, a year before the presidential election
note: a July 2026 suspension over drafting defects is the prior value, not a competing one; the vote followed a cyberattack on the incumbent operator in late July and came days after the online-falsehoods law entered into force. In January 2026 the national bar association told the Assembly that the bill required integral reformulation, objecting that the proposed cybersecurity centre would combine regulation, rule-making, supervision, inspection and sanction in one body in breach of the separation of powers, that allowing access to private communications on a judicial or administrative decision was constitutionally unacceptable, and that undefined terms invited arbitrary enforcement

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital government bill
milestone: Public consultation opened 2026-05-06
position_start: No framework law; sector rules dispersed since 1997
position_end: In public consultation, framed expressly around ending legislative dispersion and keeping the digital law and the data-protection law in step
note: no draft text and no tabling date held

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic signature and certification regime
milestone: Legislative authorisation approved unanimously 2026-07-30
position_start: A public-key and time-stamp infrastructure announced by the ministry with no legislation, date or location
position_end: Authorisation granted to the President, valid 90 days after publication of the enabling law; the substantive text will be an executive instrument defining an accrediting authority, a root certification entity and the evidential weight of a signature
note: grounded on the insufficiency of two 2011 instruments

subject: gov.legislate
name: False information law (Lei n.º 6/26)
milestone: Journalists' bodies warn of inhibition of citizen journalism
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A false-information regime in force from 4 August 2026, binding telecom operators, digital platforms and application providers, reaching content aimed at the domestic public from outside the country, and banning inauthentic accounts. On 22 August 2026 the journalists' union, the professional credential and ethics commission and the women journalists' forum warned that the law will inhibit citizen journalism, arguing that its penalties are excessive and that whether something counts as a journalistic error will depend heavily on how the courts and the aggrieved party read it
note: the account held is a law-firm note rather than the gazetted text, and no enforcement body, penalty schedule or first action is on record; the bar association had told the Assembly in January 2026 that this bill and the cybersecurity bill should be read as a single package and both required integral reformulation; this is the same instrument as the online falsehoods law recorded separately in this section, entered from a secondary account rather than from the gazette

subject: gov.legislate
name: General electronic communications regulation
milestone: Amended and republished by Decreto Presidencial n.º 271/25, 29 December 2025
position_start: As approved by Decreto Presidencial n.º 108/16 of 25 May 2016, unamended for nine years
position_end: Rewritten and republished whole: 52 articles amended and fifteen added, supplying the criteria and procedure for periodically declaring and publishing the list of operators with significant market power, extending the perimeter to over-the-top services that substitute for, complement or compete with traditional electronic communications and to non-telecoms owners of shareable passive infrastructure — ducts, towers, poles, tunnels, fibre, power systems, railways — who must publish regulator-approved reference offers and hand the regulator 1% of the revenue from such sharing agreements, and requiring an adequate level of protection for users with special needs in defining universal service
note: no regulator decision under the new articles is on record

subject: gov.legislate
name: National cybersecurity centre
milestone: Statute published 2025-12-10; launch stated for 2026 by the telecommunications minister on 2026-08-10
position_start: Did not exist; provided for in a draft presidential decree cleared by the Council of Ministers on 27 October 2025, carrying a cyber-attack response centre and mandatory institutional incident reporting
position_end: A public institute with legal personality and administrative and financial autonomy, carrying regulatory, supervisory, inspection and sanctioning powers, an internal emergency response team and a round-the-clock operations department, retaining 30% of the fines it levies. On 2026-08-10 the telecommunications minister said the centre would be launched during 2026, to monitor digital threats, defend critical infrastructure and coordinate incident response
note: no source records it exercising any power or naming a director general; eight months after its statute the responsible minister was still describing its launch in the future tense, and the national bar association has objected that combining rule-making, supervision, inspection and sanction in one body breaches the separation of powers

subject: gov.legislate
name: Online falsehoods law
milestone: Gazetted as Lei n. 6/26, Diario da Republica I Serie n. 146, in force 4 August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: In force since 4 August 2026, gazetted as Lei n. 6/26 in Diario da Republica I Serie n. 146 after the Assembleia Nacional passed it 105-72 in May with only UNITA opposed; fines of 200-400 minimum wages, one to three years for simple publication, three to eight where it incites hatred or damages reputation, and up to ten in the aggravated case
note: no enforcement action under it anywhere in the country is held; this is the same instrument as the false information law recorded separately in this section, entered from the gazette rather than from the law-firm account

subject: gov.legislate
name: Startups law
milestone: Passed unanimously, reported 2026-03-23
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Passed, with a legal definition of a startup at an annual revenue ceiling of about US$3.5m and no minimum threshold, admitting pre-revenue ventures
note: promulgation and gazette number not held

subject: gov.protect
name: Amendment opening electoral data
milestone: Rejected in plenary 2026-06-25
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Rejected, leaving the citizen databases and the electoral registers closed to parties and citizens
note: had cleared committee in April 2026; resolved for privacy over electoral transparency

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection agency
milestone: Organic statute gazetted 2016-10-10; board of three appointed 2019-09-06
position_start: Constituted and sanctioning under the superintendence of the telecommunications minister, with a 2024 wave that included the incumbent telecoms operator
position_end: In operation, sanctioning, and now the country's regional data-governance convener, with three of the seven board seats filled, every member removable by presidential decree at any time and without stated grounds, and own revenue from the fines it levies and the fees it charges, of which it retains 60% — revenue onto which a 2021 pay decree moved most of each board member's salary from May 2024
sources: 2026-06-26-apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-crescer-tech-fast-digital-center|2016-10-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-214-16-estatuto-organico-apd|2019-09-06-angola-decreto-presidencial-277-19-nomeacao-conselho-administracao-apd|2021-03-10-angola-decreto-presidencial-60-21-regulamento-taxas-apd|2021-05-25-angola-decreto-presidencial-126-21-estatuto-remuneratorio-apd|2024-08-10 Angola - Dados Pessoais e Ciber-seguranca (APD enforcement)
note: the four seats the National Assembly and the judiciary elect are not established as ever having been filled

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection agency organic law
milestone: Drafting consultancy tendered, April 2026
position_end: Drafting of the Agência de Protecção de Dados' organic law put out under a simplified contracting procedure by the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa, financed through the Projecto de Aceleração Digital de Angola
note: the agency is already operating; the base holds no organic law for it

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law
milestone: In force since 17 June 2011
position_start: In force since 2011, with consent and notification duties, sensitive-data limits and transfer approvals, and prior authorisation dispensed with wherever the processing derives from a statute or decree
position_end: In force and unamended, with fines of USD 75,000 to 150,000 and USD 65,000 to 130,000 on individuals, trebled for legal persons and materially cumulated across concurrent contraventions; article 35(6) substitutes a statute or decree for the regulator's authorisation, article 24 does the same for database interconnection, and article 4(2)(a) puts processing under state-secrecy, state-security and judicial-secrecy rules outside the law altogether
sources: 2011-06-17-angola-lei-22-11-proteccao-de-dados-pessoais|2026-07-29-angola-idea-forum-recommends-policy-harmonisation|2011-09-19 Angola Passes Personal Data Protection Law (Law 22-11)
note: a legal person's ceiling is USD 450,000; the figure the wiki previously carried was the individual ceiling

subject: gov.protect
name: Data protection law revision
milestone: Public consultation completed, announced 2026-06-17
position_end: Consultation closed on a revision adding a data-protection officer duty for high-volume processors, stronger oversight and sanction mechanisms, and redenominating fines into local currency; due at the Council of Ministers then the National Assembly
note: no draft text held

subject: gov.protect
name: Judicial oversight regime for state surveillance
status: Implemented, electronic surveillance only and no rule for intelligence access to identity data
milestone: Lei n.º 11/20 gazetted 2020-04-23
position_start: In force since April 2020: cellular location and electronic surveillance authorised in writing by the Ministério Público where the premises are private or restricted, and by the head of the police body in urgent cases with notice to the prosecutor within 72 hours
position_end: Unchanged; no judicial warrant is required at any stage, execution runs 90 days renewable once for cellular location and successively for electronic surveillance until instruction closes, private persons and businesses must open their own video-surveillance systems to the criminal police in real time or deferred, and the data-protection authority is given knowledge and monitoring of the resulting police database rather than authorisation; separately, no rule states when the intelligence service may obtain identity, biometric or mobility data, and no independent body reviews such requests
sources: 2020-04-23-angola-lei-11-20-vigilancia-electronica|2026-02-26-sinse-adquiriu-spyware-predator-para-espiar-jornalista|2025-10-08 Data protection and cybersecurity laws in Angola (CMS guide)|2026-08-15-angola-intelwatch-biometric-surveillance-report
note: the only evidence of use on file is a forensic confirmation that an intelligence service acquired commercial spyware and that it infected a journalist's phone

subject: gov.protect
name: Published data-protection fines
milestone: A third fine published 2026-08-19
position_start: A 2024 sanctions wave published, with no totals held
position_end: Over Kz 600m across two firms, plus a US$115,000 penalty against a hotel in August 2026, following two earlier fines divulged in September 2025
sources: 2026-08-19-sapo-angola-apd-fine-hotel-diamante|2026-06-26-apd-aplica-multas-milionarias-crescer-tech-fast-digital-center|2024-08-10 Angola - Dados Pessoais e Ciber-seguranca (APD enforcement)
note: deliberation texts and deliberation dates are not published, and the newest penalty is reported in dollars rather than kwanza, so the running total cannot be stated in one currency from the record. The enforcement is now reaching ordinary commercial data controllers outside the technology sector

subject: gov.protect
name: Video-surveillance licensing regime
milestone: Regulation gazetted 2021-12-21
position_start: In force since December 2021: installations licensed by the minister responsible for public security on an application filed with the National Police, carrying a prior opinion of the data-protection authority, with the police holding the national database of installed systems and carrying out inspection
position_end: Unchanged; recordings are erased at 30 days unless a criminal-police or judicial body has requested them, technical specification is mandated down to the camera housing and encryption, and authorisation fees are split 40% to the State, 35% to the National Police and 25% to the data-protection authority, with fines split 40% Treasury, 40% police and 20% authority
note: implements Lei n.º 2/20 and names the Centro Integrado de Segurança Pública as the public-security integration body

subject: gov.regional
name: African Union cybersecurity and data protection convention
milestone: Approved by Resolução n.º 33/19
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection approved by resolution of the National Assembly
note: no deposit of an instrument of ratification is on record

subject: gov.regional
name: Bilateral memorandum with a Lusophone regulator
milestone: Signed at a global privacy assembly 2025-09-18
position_start: No bilateral with any non-African regulator held
position_end: In force, providing mutual assistance and technical, regulatory and supervisory cooperation
note: a stated intention to conclude a similar arrangement elsewhere is unevidenced

subject: gov.regional
name: CPLP digital rights charter
milestone: Signed at São Tomé by all nine member states, 19 July 2024
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Expressly declaratory and non-binding, committing members to meaningful connectivity on non-discriminatory and affordable terms, personal data protection, cybersecurity cooperation, digital literacy and capacity building and non-fragmentation of the digital environment, and condemning blanket internet shutdowns; signed for Angola by the Minister of State and Chief of the Civil House
note: declaratory: no domestic measure is recorded as taken under it

subject: gov.regional
name: Export of national satellite capacity to neighbouring states
milestone: Proof-of-concept testing begun with a Mozambican operator
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Mozambique's state operator has begun proof-of-concept testing of the Angolan satellite for providing telecommunications services in Mozambique, announced by the Angolan telecommunications ministry as a step towards a commercial agreement to distribute communication and broadcasting signals over Angolan space infrastructure; it follows the Mozambican public broadcaster's own proof of concept transmitting its television signal via the satellite and implements a bilateral memorandum signed in June 2026, and runs in parallel with a commercial pilot agreement with a Namibian operator for satellite-driven backhaul
note: both trials are framed as advancing the ICT priority of the SADC regional infrastructure development master plan; no commercial terms are published

subject: gov.standards
name: Artificial intelligence readiness score
milestone: Preliminary findings presented to the ministry 2026-06-30
position_end: 50.9% of indicators fully ready, 32.7% partially ready and 16% insufficient, with data governance at 47 out of 100 and science-workforce availability at about 12%
note: the widely quoted higher figure is the first two bands added together, not a readiness score

subject: gov.standards
name: Hydrocarbon data delivery regulation
milestone: Decreto Executivo n.º 691/25, 29 August 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Associates of the national oil agency and credentialed service companies must deliver all geophysical, well and geospatial hydrocarbon data to the agency's data management and archive office in prescribed formats and by set deadlines — six months where special laboratory analysis is done outside Angola — and submit within three months a full inventory of every physical sample held in the country or abroad, together with reports of any analyses performed overseas
note: a sectoral data-delivery mandate with no published compliance record

subject: gov.standards
name: National standards body
milestone: 2026 national standards catalogue posted 9 March 2026
position_start: Formed by the 2021 merger of the standardisation and accreditation institutes (Decreto Presidencial n.º 95/21 of 20 April 2021)
position_end: An ISO correspondent member publishing a 2026 national standards catalogue that incorporates 140 new standards, including texts arising from SADC regional harmonisation covering the circular economy, construction and building materials, food, quality management, safety rules, technology suppliers, occupational health and safety and vehicle safety; the institute states that Angolan standards are voluntary and are made mandatory only by legislation in the public interest
note: correspondent membership carries no vote on ISO technical work

subject: gov.standards
name: Territorial unit codification
milestone: Lei n.º 8/25, 16 September 2025
position_start: Codification under Lei n.º 8/16 of 15 June 2016, overtaken by the 2024 redrawing of the political-administrative map
position_end: A single national codification: unique sequential alphanumeric codes for the country (AO), its 21 provinces, 326 municipalities and 378 communes, on criteria the law states are drawn from ISO standards expressly to ease data exchange between national and international systems, with codes vacated by an abolished unit left permanently unassigned
note: no published code list or register is held

subject: finance.budget
name: Authorisation for an integrated ecosystem of state digital services
milestone: Authorised 2026-08-31
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: US$210.91m authorised by the president for an integrated ecosystem of state digital services, alongside US$13m for a public administration interoperability platform and US$4.6m to strengthen state cybersecurity

subject: finance.budget
name: Communications programme appropriation
milestone: 2026 budget appropriation down 30.5%
position_start: Kz 229.3bn appropriated for 2025
position_end: Kz 159.2bn appropriated for 2026, of which fourth-generation expansion is Kz 62.7bn, down 42%, with the third-generation coverage line deleted
note: no released, actual or audited figure held for either year

subject: finance.budget
name: Ministry budget execution
milestone: First per-organ execution table published
position_start: None published; the wiki held no released, actual or audited line for any digital stem
position_end: 3% first-quarter execution, with 20 of 50 programmes below 5%
note: the per-organ report itself is not held and sits on the acquisitions list

subject: finance.budget
name: Supplementary credit for identity-card universalisation
milestone: Gazetted 2025-09-19
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: US$218,500,000 of supplementary credit assigned to the justice ministry, released against payment need and treasury availability
note: the decree states the amount in US dollars, with no local-currency equivalent

subject: finance.budget
name: Supplementary credit for the citizen-database update
milestone: A presidential order reported 2026-02-26
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: US$275,000,000 opened inside the 2026 budget, more than doubling the territorial administration ministry's allocation, for the adult-citizen database proof-of-life update
note: the gazetted order is not held, only reporting

subject: finance.new
name: Civil registration and local governance project
milestone: Post rehabilitation reported 2026-04-06
position_start: US$250m of financing launched in 2023 across eight provinces and 53 municipalities
position_end: Eleven birth-registration posts rehabilitated in one province with five operating since August 2025, thirteen more nearing completion in another, and mass registration campaigns reaching several thousand people

subject: finance.new
name: Digital acceleration project
milestone: Third steering committee 2026-07-30
position_start: A US$300m loan signed 2024-10-11 and effective from 2025-05-08 after a 90-day extension, with US$0 disbursed against it and both World Bank ratings cut to Moderately Unsatisfactory in April 2025
position_end: US$112.21m of the US$300m disbursed at 10 June 2026, 37.40%, with both World Bank ratings lifted to Moderately Satisfactory and every project outcome indicator reading 0 as at 30 April 2026 against March 2030 targets of 13,500,000 people using broadband internet, 10,000,000 with digitally verifiable identification, 100,000 trained through digital literacy programmes and 400 firms adopting digital technologies; the steering committee separately reports a national broadband stock of 14,743,807 rising to 19.7 million by 2030
note: the terms are not concessional, carrying a front-end fee and a variable spread, and the Bank's broadband indicator counts only people the project itself connects rather than the national stock; the project's own terms of reference show what the disbursement is buying — implementation and training for the Public Administration Interoperability Platform, a national policy for the management and hosting of public data, a digital-government and public-sector artificial-intelligence governance framework, the organic law of the data-protection agency, digital-skills and connectivity specialists, and e-learning for the public-administration school — and its safeguards plan commits Component 2 to a shared data-governance framework, shared infrastructure, an open-data portal and electronic services

subject: finance.new
name: Health emergency preparedness project
milestone: Appraised 4 November 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A US$253m operation carrying a named and separately costed health-data architecture: subcomponent 1.4, information systems for health emergencies, at IBRD US$4.5m plus a US$0.5m grant, funding vital-statistics completeness for births and deaths linked to DHIS2, immunisation registries and surveillance systems and platforms integrating public-health surveillance, laboratory, environmental-health, service-disruption and veterinary data; and subcomponent 2.1 at IBRD US$32m for national guidance and standard operating procedures for integrated disease surveillance and response, routine and event-based surveillance focused on the Lobito Corridor, and epidemic-intelligence functions
note: an appraisal document; no signature, effectiveness or disbursement is on file

subject: finance.new
name: Mobility fintech investment
milestone: Investment announced 2026-06-26
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Proparco invested, amount undisclosed
note: the financier discloses no amount, instrument, tenor or stake

subject: finance.new
name: Private credit fund
milestone: Second deployment announced March 2026
position_end: The country's first private-credit vehicle for small and mid-market firms, anchored by a US$5m sovereign-fund commitment in 2024, with two deployments to date
note: no fund size or investor list beyond the anchor

subject: finance.new
name: Public security innovation project
milestone: Phase two broke ground 2026-02-12, due 2028
position_start: Named in the National Police strategic development plan for 2022-2027, whose principal axis is integrated police information platforms; the force's personnel and cadre system holding close to 100,000 records entered production in 2023, the private network was fully installed to provincial commands and half installed to central bodies, and phase two's five Luanda municipal centres — Cazenga, Cacuaco, Kilamba Kiaxi, Talatona and Viana — were identified but not begun
position_end: Five municipal command and control centres under construction, USD 87m
note: financed by the Export-Import Bank of Korea; the commitment date is not established, and no data-protection basis, retention rule or supervisory authority is named for the camera estate

subject: infra.connect
name: 2Africa Angola branch
milestone: Landing station inaugurated and service switched on 2025-12-13
position_start: Not in service; the cable had berthed but the branch and landing station were still being built
position_end: In service on a US$43m operator-built branch, with 23.6 Tbps of the cable's capacity allocated to Angola, replacing an end-of-life system and one at capacity
note: the incumbent is the only Angolan member of the consortium

subject: infra.connect
name: Africell network in Cabinda
milestone: 20 towers installed, commercial service days away (2026-08-19)
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: 20 telecom towers installed and satellite backhaul agreed, with commercial voice, data and satellite-linked service stated as starting within days
note: the operator's third-network entry reaching an exclave province, with backhaul tied to satellite capacity under an agreement with the national space programme office GGPEN; no coverage percentage, investment figure, population reached or launch date is published, and 'in the coming days' is the whole of the commitment held

subject: infra.connect
name: Digital terrestrial television transition
milestone: Agreement signed August 2025 at about US$10m
position_start: Did not exist as a financed project
position_end: About US$10m of foreign financing modernising transmitters at three sites, motivated partly by disaster-alert broadcasting; no progress or switchover date published since
note: twelve months with nothing on file

subject: infra.connect
name: Domestic submarine cable
milestone: Restated by the telecommunications minister, 2 September 2026
position_end: A planned domestic cable to interlink the coastal cities and connect a transport corridor to an international system, restated by the telecommunications minister on 2 September 2026 as being prepared to link the coastal cities' networks and support the terrestrial fibre network, within a programme to extend fibre services to the whole national territory. The minister said the ministry is developing partnerships with private operators and public companies for fibre expansion, that connections to neighbouring countries are also planned, and that the objective is to make the country a regional technology hub; no route, cost, financier or date is published
note: six months on from the first statement the project has the same content and no more: what changed is the framing, not the plan

subject: infra.connect
name: Enterprise 5G service
milestone: Commercial launch in Cabinda 2026-07-23
position_start: Phase-one technical specifications being finalised, not commercially launched
position_end: Commercially launched in Cabinda, with Luanda at over 70% city coverage, about US$20m budgeted and every provincial capital targeted by 2027
note: enterprise connectivity, not consumer mobile, and the throughput figures are the operator's own

subject: infra.connect
name: Equiano capacity through Namibia
milestone: Master service agreement signed 2026-06-12
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The state operator to receive an initial 1.0 Tbps of dedicated capacity through a Namibian landing, with an option to assume ownership; design, testing, commissioning and handover still to run
note: Angola reaches this cable only indirectly

subject: infra.connect
name: Fifth-generation standalone network
milestone: Trial standalone data call completed in a live environment
position_start: Core transformation completed and a standalone trial call done, with no commercial launch
position_end: Unchanged; no held source records a commercial standalone launch date
note: a vendor release

subject: infra.connect
name: Internet exchange points
milestone: Tracker reading for June 2026
position_end: Two active internet exchange points with 29 members between them, present in one of the fourteen population centres above 300,000
note: a third-party tracker reading; the base holds no earlier count

subject: infra.connect
name: Low-orbit satellite licence
milestone: Multi-year capacity agreement signed 2026-06-12
position_start: A 15-year licence granted in June 2025 with a Luanda ground station, first and only licensed low-orbit operator, no commercial offtake on file
position_end: Licence held and now commercially deployed through a multi-year capacity agreement with a local provider

subject: infra.connect
name: National broadband network
milestone: Specific loan agreement signed October 2023 at about US$249m
position_start: Financed and active, with no delivery milestone published
position_end: Financed and active, still with no delivery milestone
note: a Chinese concessional loan with no progress report on file at either end; the ICT White Paper 2023-2027, brought into force by Decreto Presidencial n.º 272/24, is where the country's broadband programme sits, in place of any free-standing national broadband plan

subject: infra.connect
name: National terrestrial fibre length
milestone: No authoritative series; five official statements run non-monotonic
position_start: Already inconsistent at 22,000 km in 2023, itself an older figure, against a recurring 2,000 km annual increment
position_end: 22,000 km in 2023, 20,000 in October 2025, 30,000 in November 2025, 22,000 in April 2026 and 28,000 in June 2026; the wiki asserts no current national figure
note: the regulator's annual statistical report that would settle it was dropped as unobtainable

subject: infra.connect
name: Operator fibre network in Benguela
milestone: Inaugurated by the telecommunications ministry, 2 September 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Inaugurated along the Benguela coastline, with the minister naming nationwide fibre coverage as the objective for the segment and disclosing that a submarine cable landing at Benguela is being prepared

subject: infra.connect
name: Rural roaming and infrastructure-sharing programme
milestone: A tower commissioned in Moxico June 2026
position_end: National roaming and infrastructure sharing with shared towers, solar power and satellite backhaul, extending voice and data to remote areas
note: no national site count, budget or target published

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink licence
milestone: Licensing process open since 2024 and unresolved
position_start: Unlicensed, with the ministry saying only that negotiations were continuing
position_end: Unlicensed; a secretary of state says only that the process is under way, and the regulator is still working out how to fit low-orbit operators into a regime written for terrestrial networks
note: sixteen months of identical status is the finding

subject: infra.connect
name: Universal and meaningful connectivity indicators
milestone: 2024 indicators published at an ITU workshop, 5-7 November 2025
position_start: 42.10% of individuals using the internet (2022) and 48.80% (2023)
position_end: 55.50% of individuals using the internet in 2024, 12,785,472 broadband subscriptions at 36.40% penetration against 26,407,932 mobile subscriptions at 75.19%, and national population coverage of 89.60% (2G), 85.66% (3G), 77.41% (4G) and 16.40% (5G), with 5G reaching only Luanda, Benguela and Huambo of the then eighteen provinces and Luanda alone at 100% on 2G, 3G and 4G
note: the regulator's own series, reported to the ITU

subject: infra.store
name: Commercial data centre
position_start: Did not exist; the country had no Tier III commercial data centre
position_end: Operating at up to 3 MW and more than 800 racks over 19,000 square metres on US$30m, near the cable landings, with a plan to exceed 7 MW within five years
sources: 2025-10-02 Raxio Opens Angola's Largest Data Centre in Landmark 30 Million Expansion|2026-07-23-raxio-afr-ix-data-centres-angola-mozambique
