subject: infra.store
name: Government data centre
milestone: Government cloud backup centre reinaugurated after modernisation, 25 August 2026
position_start: Under construction at about 75% complete, operation expected in the first half of 2026
position_end: The government cloud's backup centre was reinaugurated after modernisation at 48 racks, framed by the minister as reinforcing digital sovereignty
sources: 2026-08-25-pti-angola-centro-backup-cloud-governo-48-racks|2026-08-25-angop-infosi-backup-data-center-requalificacao|2026-04-28-pr-inaugura-novo-centro-de-dados-do-governo|2025-11-14 Angola Nears Completion of National Data Center, Set for 2026 Launch|2026-05-21-ggpen-angosat-2-national-data-center-redundancy
note: the rack count and the sovereignty framing are the ministry's own, and no capacity, occupancy, cost or recovery-time objective for the backup is published; the space agency separately states that ANGOSAT-2 provides redundancy and service continuity for the centre, the first published account of an off-site continuity path

subject: infra.store
name: National cloud
milestone: Launched with the government data centre 2026-04-28
position_start: First stone laid September 2025, with a migration mandate stated and nothing yet to migrate onto
position_end: A unified government cloud in operation under a progressive and mandatory migration of public services, framed as repatriating passports and education certificates from foreign platforms
sources: 2026-04-28-centro-de-dados-do-governo-soberania-digital|2025-09-10 Angola advances technological development for digital transformation|2023-02-16-minttics-infosi-projecto-cloud-nacional-dois-data-centers
note: no source records how much has actually migrated; the project was presented by the information-society institute in February 2023 as a US$89m investment in national cloud infrastructure and two data centres

subject: infra.store
name: Operator data centre at Lobito
milestone: Installed as the platform behind the Benguela fibre network
position_start: No account held
position_end: Installed at a Lobito development as the technical support and data-management platform for the operator's internet and television services along the coastline; no capacity figure is published

subject: infra.store
name: Public data management and hosting policy
milestone: Strategic and legal consultancy tendered, March 2026
position_end: A national policy for the management and hosting of public data, with its regulation, put out to consultancy by the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa under the Projecto de Aceleração Digital de Angola
note: the policy text is not held and the base carries no earlier position on public-data hosting

subject: infra.store
name: Second commercial data centre project
milestone: Announced 2023-06-27 with a US$31m facility in November 2023
position_start: Announced as the country's first Tier IV facility at over 10 MW and 2,000 racks, financed but not built
position_end: Unchanged; no source since 2023 and no completion date was ever stated
sources: 2023-06-27 Paratus to build third Angola data center (DC3, Tier IV)
note: three years of silence on the only Tier IV project in the country

subject: infra.energy
name: Household access to electricity
milestone: Census definitive results published 2025-11-20
position_start: 31.9% of households in the 2014 census
position_end: 48.6% of households at the 2024 census reference date, 68.9% urban and 8.5% rural
sources: 2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos|2023-07-04 AD664 - Lack of grid access plagues most rural residents in Angola
note: the physical floor under every named object in this section

subject: infra.energy
name: HYDRO-LINK Angola-DRC cross-border transmission line
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed 14 October 2025 at the USA-DRC Economic and Investments Forum
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A 1,150 km, US$1.5bn, 1,200MW line to carry surplus Angolan hydropower to the DRC, targeted for completion in 2029 and aimed principally at the Copperbelt mining sector; the memorandum is between HYDRO-LINK and the DRC government, and no Angolan offtake, tariff or financing close is published
note: Angola is the source of the power and not a party to the memorandum on the record.

subject: infra.energy
name: Power Sector Action Plan electrification target
milestone: Target year passed with no published outturn
position_start: A target of 60% electrification by 2025, from 47% in 2020, still open
position_end: The target year passed, with the only later dated measure a different one and no electrification rate published since the 2020 baseline
sources: 2023-07-04 AD664 - Lack of grid access plagues most rural residents in Angola|2025-11-20-ine-angola-censo-2024-relatorio-sintese-resultados-definitivos|2016-07-22-minea-angola-energia-2025-visao-longo-prazo-sector-electrico|2021-01-21-world-bank-pad3510-angola-electricity-sector-improvement-and-access
note: the 2025 target comes from the sector's own long-term vision, Angola Energia 2025; a US$250m World Bank electricity sector improvement and access loan was appraised in January 2021, and no electrification rate has been published against either

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Compensation for the incumbent's July 2026 cyberattack
milestone: Automatic compensation announced August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The incumbent said it will compensate customers automatically for the July 2026 cyberattack that cut its services nationwide - business customers credited on their August or September invoice and consumer accounts given extra days of service, with no request needed. Mobile voice, messaging, data and internet are restored bar call waiting, and the operator's investigation with independent external specialists has found no evidence so far of any compromise or improper access to customer or partner personal data
note: the operator's own account; no regulator finding or breach notification is on file

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Critical national infrastructure designation
milestone: No designation instrument in force
position_start: None published
position_end: Named analysts argued after a national mobile outage that telecommunications should be designated critical alongside power and water; the operator dates the attack to the early hours of 2026-07-28 and states that voice, messaging, mobile data, internet access and third-party services over its network were restored on 2026-08-05, nine days later; no instrument exists, and the bill that would supply the designation is still a proposal
note: enactment of the cybersecurity law, or a standalone decree, would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cyber-security appropriation
milestone: US$4.6m authorised 2026-08-31
position_start: Kz 70.5bn in the 2025 budget, about US$76.4m at the source's stated rate
position_end: US$4.6m authorised by the president to strengthen state cybersecurity, against an appropriation that had fallen
note: read at draft stage before enactment

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Cybersecurity fund
milestone: Presupposed by the cyber centre's statute, established by nothing on file
position_end: The statute splits the centre's receipts three ways including a share to a cybersecurity fund, which is created and governed by no instrument the wiki holds
note: a constitutive decree would settle it

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Financial sector cyber and cloud rules
milestone: Aviso n.º 8/20, 2 April 2020
position_start: In force
position_end: In force, unamended: rules on cyber-security policy and on the terms and conditions of contracting data-processing, data-storage and cloud-computing services, binding on the institutions the central bank supervises
note: the only sectoral cyber rule the base holds, and it predates every national cyber instrument

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Recovery from the July 2026 attack on the incumbent mobile operator
milestone: Core services declared fully restored nationwide 2026-08-21
position_start: Voice, messaging, data and internet services degraded nationwide following the 2026-07-28 attack
position_end: Voice, messaging, data, internet and third-party network services declared fully restored nationwide, with only the custom ringback-tone feature still offline; a continuing forensic investigation with independent external experts has found no evidence of unauthorised access to or sharing of customer or partner personal data, and affected users are receiving automatic invoice credits or additional service days
note: the operator's own account; the forensic investigation is stated as continuing, no attacker, vector or outage cost is published, and no regulator finding is held

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Citizen-database interoperability commission
milestone: A presidential decree created an interministerial commission 2026-06-08
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A commission to stabilise civil-identification and adult-citizen database interoperability, biometrically de-duplicate, update residence and consolidate the electoral base, with a US$275m supplementary credit
note: no technical standard, interface or completion date is on file

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Land rights single window
milestone: Launched 16 September 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The Janela Única de Concessão de Direitos Fundiários, under which a citizen lodges a land-concession file once at the municipal administration and the state then routes it through the tax authority, the geographic and cadastral institute and the property-registry conservatories, the product of four years of joint work across ministries
note: no throughput, coverage or processing-time figure has been published since launch

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Logistics single window
milestone: Phase one expected between the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027
position_start: Did not exist; the port, foreign-trade and customs platforms ran separately
position_end: An integrated ecosystem to absorb three separate agency platforms into one, framed explicitly as a formalisation and tax-base instrument rather than trade facilitation
note: a board communique is the only source; no instrument, budget or vendor named

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Public administration interoperability platform
milestone: US$13m authorised 2026-08-31
position_start: Provided for by the Plano Nacional da Arquitectura Global para a Interoperabilidade na Administração Central e Local do Estado (Decreto Presidencial n.º 46/18 of 14 February 2018); not built
position_end: US$13m authorised by presidential order for the platform
note: a flagship project of the digital transition agenda; no supplier, contract award or go-live is on record

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Public digital infrastructure contract
milestone: Execution opened 2026-07-31
position_start: Did not exist; no national interoperability platform in service
position_end: US$150m over a twelve-month execution period for a secure-zone critical-computing component hosting the interoperability platform, key-based electronic signatures, digital identity and structured cybersecurity; in execution from 2026-07-31, financed under Despacho Presidencial n.º 38/26 and inscribed in the 2026 public investment programme
note: a sole-referenced state technology award under a presidential order, procurement route unstated

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Tax-compliance certificate interoperability
milestone: Customs clearance automated for compliant taxpayers, stated 2026-02-10
position_start: None published
position_end: Automated inside the tax authority; extension to banks and other state bodies under way
note: the enforcement side is already live - a taxpayer not invoicing electronically cannot be paid by the State - while the interoperability it rests on is still being built

subject: dpi.id
name: At-home identity-card service
milestone: Launched 2026-07-28, first phase in one province only
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Kz 250,000 for at-home processing and Kz 10,000 for at-home delivery alone, on a 48-hour issuance target, with requests through a web portal and a messaging number
note: the ministry called the fee a product of exclusivity, and no ministry publication naming the portal is on file

subject: dpi.id
name: Biometric electronic passport
milestone: First two issued 2026-03-10
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Issued across all 21 provinces by end-March 2026 and to the diaspora from May 2026
note: no issuance volume or backlog figure published

subject: dpi.id
name: Civil and criminal identification bill
milestone: Approved by the Council of Ministers 2026-04-29
position_start: Did not exist; voter cards, driving licences and passports accepted as substitutes
position_end: Would make the identity card the only valid document for banking, telecoms, school enrolment, property registration and contracts, and set the country's first dedicated identity-data-processing regime
note: no parliamentary stage recorded since April 2026

subject: dpi.id
name: Identity card coverage
milestone: Census definitive results published 2025-11-20
position_start: No national coverage figure published; a 2023 diagnostic states only that the country is far from universal coverage
position_end: 52.4% of the population aged five and over hold the card, 63% urban against 30.9% rural, leaving 14.9m people undocumented
note: the movement is in measurement, not in coverage

subject: dpi.id
name: National biometric border-control system
status: In development, one border post operating
milestone: Independent fact-check separates the confirmed from the alleged
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: Budgeted at US$112m and awarded in February 2025 to a consortium of a local company and a Polish technology firm, reportedly by direct award rather than open tender, using fingerprint and facial recognition; the interior ministry announced the consignment record on 25 February 2025. No biometric system operates at the border posts with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and one post is functional. A national fact-checking outlet assessed the surveillance report this record rests on and rated the project's existence and the consignment confirmed, the claim that the local contractor had no biometrics track record not independently verified, the alleged personal interest of the interior minister in the contract not proven - it rests on anonymous interviews with no corporate, judicial or financial documents - and the link between a change of suppliers at the migration service and the electronic-passport issuance backlog partially confirmed, the minister himself having acknowledged the backlog in September 2025
note: the fact-check is the more careful document of the two and is what this row now rests on: it holds the procurement facts and drops the conflict-of-interest allegation, which no document supports

subject: dpi.id
name: National identity card
milestone: Issuing on a foreign-built platform since 2017
position_start: In issue, one of several accepted identity documents, coverage unmeasured
position_end: In issue nationwide and generated from the birth record by system interoperability, with coverage now measured and sole-identity status pending in a 2026 bill
note: the credential is unchanged; what moved is its measurement and its proposed legal monopoly

subject: dpi.id
name: Registo Eleitoral Oficioso 2026-2027
milestone: Update brigades deployed to a pilgrimage site 29 August to 6 September 2026
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: Voter-register update brigades stationed at the Muxima sanctuary from 29 August to 6 September 2026, run through the single public service counter, with pilgrims needing an identity card or voter card to take part; the register's national director stated on 28 August 2026 that more than a million citizens are enrolled to vote in the 2027 general election
note: no target enrolment, budget or completion date for the register update is stated

subject: dpi.id
name: Single digital identity
milestone: US$28m authorised and public tender opened by Despacho Presidencial 300/26 of 2026-08-13
position_start: Named as a workstream in the 2024 World Bank loan agreement, nothing built
position_end: Procurement opened: the President authorised US$28m for a National Digital Identity and Electronic Signatures Platform and formally opened the public tender by Despacho Presidencial 300/26 of 13 August 2026, the platform specified to support up to 30 million digital identities and to let citizens, firms and public officials use a single digital credential for public services, digital contracts, electronic identity verification of customers and legally valid electronic signatures. The target architecture was set out to the African registrars' meeting in July 2026: a multifunctional database under the Ministério da Justiça merging the civil-registry, identity-card, criminal-record, vehicle, commercial, land and notarial systems across three phases, with biographic and biometric data — fingerprints, facial photograph, iris and biometric signature — captured at birth registration and at identity-card issue, and a Número Único do Cidadão assigned as the structuring identifier from the first weeks of life
note: distinct from the identity card; the specification is as recited in the despacho, no supplier or timetable is stated, and the civil-registry code being amended to carry the architecture is still the 1967 colonial text

subject: dpi.id
name: Taxpayer identification number
milestone: Register operations codified in the tax offices' procedures manual, version 2.0
position_start: A legal regime for the attribution, composition and use of the taxpayer number (Decreto Presidencial n.º 245/21 of 4 October 2021), with the tax offices applying divergent procedures and treating comparable cases differently
position_end: Issue, update, suspension and cessation of the taxpayer number codified as an administered process inside the integrated tax-management system, with case flow routed through an enterprise content management system and register transactions taken through the taxpayer portal
note: the divergence finding is the tax authority's own, stated as the reason for the rewrite

subject: dpi.id
name: Unique student identifier
milestone: Decreto Presidencial n.º 227/25, 14 November 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The Identificador Único do Aluno defined as an alphanumeric code carrying a pupil's personal data and full school and assessment history, with every accredited institution required to load that assessment history, and its record of certificate holders, into a Plataforma Nacional de Certificação — which requests, issues, verifies and stores school certificates under a QR code — within 30 days of each school year's end
note: no source records the platform operating or the identifier being issued, and no data-protection basis is stated for a code carrying a pupil's full assessment history

subject: dpi.pay
name: Financial inclusion rate
milestone: Scorecard given by a state minister 2026-07-09
position_start: 51% of the population financially excluded and only 25% with a good level of financial literacy (2024-12), on the figures the draft strategy was written against
position_end: 51.7% at the first quarter of 2026 against a 65% target for 2027, with banking at 32% or 5.7m people and mobile and digital payments up about 56% year on year
note: the pre-strategy baseline is the draft strategy's own, and the two ends are not stated on the same measure

subject: dpi.pay
name: Instant payment scheme
milestone: Monthly operator report for February 2026
position_start: 35m transfers and Kz 590bn over 2025 across 22 banking and non-banking institutions
position_end: Wallet-led and concentrated, with the largest wallet at 52.2% of transfers, more than 12.3m registered accounts and about 24.8m active payment keys, and 66.4% of transfers under Kz 10,000
note: the base holds no launch date and no figure dated before 2025

subject: dpi.pay
name: Kwanza as a regional settlement currency
milestone: Formally introduced by the two central-bank governors 2026-07-27
position_start: Not a settlement currency; the regional system had cleared in one currency since 2013
position_end: The second settlement currency in the system's history, against 2025 trade and interbank flows with the other fourteen member states of about US$3.77bn across nine currencies

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment services authorisation regime
milestone: Non-bank acquirer rules set by Aviso n.º 1/26, 28 January 2026
position_start: Access to payment-services activity regulated under Aviso n.º 2/22 of 2 February 2022
position_end: Rebuilt in two steps: Aviso n.º 4/25 of 22 August 2025 set rules for opening, operating and closing electronic-money accounts, defining four account types graded by how the holder proves identity and opening them to resident nationals and foreigners, to under-18s on a parental responsibility term, to non-resident foreigners with legal stay and to micro and small companies, revoking articles 11 and 14 to 17 of the 2022 aviso; and Aviso n.º 1/26 of 28 January 2026 repealed the 2022 acquiring rules and required every non-bank acquirer of payment terminals or ATMs to be a payment service provider authorised by the central bank, certified under the Multicaixa arrangement and holding a float account at a bank, bringing sub-acquirers under named risk, settlement and contractual-transparency duties
note: no register of authorised non-bank providers is published

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment system value limits
milestone: Instrutivo n.º 02/2025, in force 30 days after publication
position_start: Limits set by Instrutivo n.º 09/24 of 19 December 2024
position_end: Standardised cheques capped at Kz 9,999,999.99, Multicaixa payments at Kz 30m a day, credit transfers at Kz 50m and direct-debit instructions at Kz 30m per operation, with real-time gross settlement compulsory above Kz 50m and a business-to-government carve-out giving the finance ministry, the social-security institute and the central bank a Kz 99,999,999.99 Multicaixa per-operation ceiling and outright exemption from the transfer and direct-debit limits
note: the state's exemption from the limits set for everyone else is written into the instrument

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payments messaging standard migration
milestone: Migration completed 2026-07-10, announced 2026-07-16
position_end: Domestic payments migrated to the international messaging standard across the switch, the exchange and the real-time settlement participants
note: only the completion is dated; no programme start, scope document or cost is held

subject: dpi.registry
name: Beneficial ownership register
milestone: Approved in committee 12 May 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A bill of 56 articles in five chapters with an annexed schedule of fines, approved by the National Assembly's committees on 12 May 2026, setting rules for identifying, registering, updating and disclosing the beneficial owners of domestic and foreign legal persons created, registered or operating in Angola and for the accessibility, management, maintenance and security of that information, framed as anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing compliance
note: no plenary vote, promulgation or register is on record

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration coverage
milestone: Census definitive results published 2025-11-20
position_start: 53.5% overall and 24.8% for children aged nought to four in the 2014 census
position_end: 63.0% overall and only 39.2% among children aged nought to four at the 2024 census reference date
note: the pipeline feeding the identity card is under-registering the newest cohort fastest

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration in maternity wards
milestone: Launched in one province 2026-03-04, running there since October 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Registry posts in maternity wards so newborns leave registered and issued a first identity card, foreign-funded with UN support
sources: 2026-03-04-zaire-inicia-registo-de-recem-nascidos-na-maternidade|2025-11-17 Angola begins issuance of ID cards to newborns
note: no national rollout map or registration count published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Circular 05/2026 on school enrolment of undocumented children
milestone: Circular signed 2026-08-19
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Every public and private school teaching primary and first-cycle secondary education is ordered to enrol children holding no birth certificate and no identity card, to mobilise families on civil registration, and to compile by the end of October 2026 a survey of undocumented pupils for the justice ministry's identification and registry directorate, whose services are then to travel to the schools and register the children
note: the education ministry says the 17-21 August 2026 enrolment round drew large numbers of school-age children with no birth registration, identity card or refugee card

subject: dpi.registry
name: Civil-registration post rehabilitation
milestone: Component rehabilitating birth-registration posts
position_start: A US$250m local-governance project across eight provinces and 53 municipalities
position_end: Eleven birth-registration posts rehabilitated in one province and thirteen in another, with mass campaigns reaching several thousand people
note: only two provinces have published delivery counts

subject: dpi.registry
name: Deconcentrated identity-card printing
milestone: All 21 provinces printing locally from 2026-07-01
position_start: Did not exist; every card printed at a single national production centre
position_end: All 21 provinces print locally, with two to three printers per province planned and a 24-to-48-hour issuance target; Cabinda issued more than 2,000 cards in just over a fortnight, and mobile brigades with portable printers and a fee-paying home-collection service are to be intensified
note: printing decentralisation only; enrolment and biometric capture are untouched

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electoral register proof-of-life operation
milestone: Opposition parties demand an independent audit of the electoral database (2026-08-19)
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: 254 of a planned 634 counters live across all 21 provinces and the diaspora, with 10,747 field workers against a target universe of 16,707,455 citizens; over 730,000 updated nationally on the opposition's count, and four opposition parties are demanding an independent audit of the database
note: the electoral administration has published no enrolment figure since the operation opened, and the only national count the base holds - over 730,000 of a 16.7m universe - comes from the opposition's own political declaration. Four parties (BD, PDP-ANA, PNSA and PPA) allege administrative discretion, uneven deployment of registration brigades and recurring biometric-system failures, and say the administration refuses to release enrolment statistics disaggregated by province, municipality and commune, which blocks any audit of the register's real flow; the electoral commission had earlier refused accreditation to the civic monitor Movimento Mudei. At provincial level the Lunda-Norte government reports over 40,000 residents updated and is pressing mining-sector workers to register through the one-stop service desks. None of the allegations has been adjudicated and no official series exists to test them against

subject: dpi.registry
name: Industrial poles digital platform
milestone: Obligation created by Decreto Legislativo Presidencial n.º 2/26, 10 February 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The industrial development and technological innovation institute is obliged to develop, run and keep current an integrated digital platform for the national network of industrial development poles, centralising concessions, transfers of land rights, lot availability and infrastructure status, with concession-holders obliged to feed it permanently
note: a statutory obligation with nothing on record being built

subject: dpi.registry
name: Official electoral registration law
milestone: Amended and republished by Lei n.º 13/25 of 1 December 2025
position_start: The Registo Eleitoral Oficioso under Lei n.º 8/15 as amended by Lei n.º 21/21, with no statutory link to the identity database and no proof-of-life update in law
position_end: Lei n.º 13/25 amends and republishes the law so that the Base de Dados de Cidadãos Maiores is fed automatically from the Bilhete de Identidade database and kept in permanent communication with it, requires its managers to interconnect it with other State data systems — passport, social-security and taxpayer bases among them — to verify identity, residence, deaths and improper entries, and adds an article 71.º-A putting the pre-election proof-of-life update on statute, to begin by the third quarter of 2026 and end 31 March 2027; in-person registration is replaced by automatic enrolment and the voter card is used for the last time in 2027, after which the Bilhete de Identidade becomes the sole registration credential
note: the statutory text is now held; no gazette number is stated in the copy on file

subject: dpi.registry
name: One-stop business registration counters
milestone: Extended beyond Luanda to Huambo, 23 June 2026
position_start: A counter network confined to Luanda
position_end: A one-stop counter opened in Cidade Baixa, Huambo, for company incorporation, alteration and legalisation and for property-registration certificates, equipped under the Diversifica+ programme and serving businesses along the Lobito Corridor and the Planalto Central
note: no incorporation count or processing time for the new counter is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Private credit information centres
milestone: No licensing instrument, operator or start date on file
position_end: The data-protection agency, working with the International Finance Corporation, explained the centres, their personal-data safeguards and their expected economic effect to journalists on 2026-08-05; no licensing instrument, named operator or start date is on file
note: an APD or central-bank licensing instrument, or a named operating centre, would settle it

subject: dpi.registry
name: Property-legalisation platform
milestone: A target of 40,000 properties legalised by end-2026 set 2026-04-17
position_start: Did not exist; the Cadastro Predial legal regime (Lei n.º 23/21 of 18 October 2021) in force with no digital route through it
position_end: A digital platform linking the cadastre, the tax authority and the property registry, aimed at cutting duplication and enabling mortgage access
note: no progress figure against the target has been published since April 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: Single social register
milestone: Field-enrolment pilot opened at Sumbe, Cuanza-Sul, 2026-08-24
position_start: Did not exist as a single register; social-transfer targeting rested on the Kwenda programme's own registry under Decreto Presidencial n.º 125/20
position_end: A single national social registry, instituted by Decreto Presidencial n.º 136/19 of 10 May 2019 and activated in its modernised and expanded form on 20 July 2026, which the social-action ministry states adds interoperability between public institutions, integration of databases and better information quality, and which underpins the Kwenda cash transfer — put at more than 1.3 million households and about 6.5 million people — and the national school-feeding programme; a US$27m component of the World Bank's Projecto de Protecção Social e Capital Humano finances the modernisation of Kwenda's delivery systems and the grievance system, targeting about 1.5 million households and 7.4 million people; field enrolment opened in a pilot phase at Sumbe in Cuanza-Sul on 2026-08-24, directed by the social-action minister, to identify and characterise Angolan families and especially those in need
note: the governing decree and the interoperability commitment are now on record; no enrolment count for the register itself and no data-protection basis is stated

subject: dpi.registry
name: Uncollected identity cards
milestone: Two statements two days apart, 15 and 17 July 2026
position_end: More than 120,000 issued cards awaiting collection at identification posts nationwide on 15 July 2026, and more than 100,000 on 17 July 2026, the second stated against general elections due in 2027
note: two statements two days apart and no series behind either; the Secretary of State for Justice separately said registration levels still fall short of the targets set

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education and research network
milestone: Presented at a national roadshow 2026-05-13
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A national education and research network presented alongside an executive roadmap for higher-education digital transformation
note: no connected institutions, capacity, funding or operating date stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: Higher education information system
milestone: Sole official submission channel from 1 October 2025
position_start: Did not exist as the official channel
position_end: The higher-education information system became the official channel from 1 October 2025 for submitting the creation of new institutions, organic units and graduate and postgraduate courses, with 75 institutions registered on the platform and more than 50 focal points from 20 public and private institutions trained
note: no submission count or processing time is published

subject: dpi.mis
name: National education database (MED and Mwango Brain)
milestone: Initiative launched in Luanda, 5-7 August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A structured multi-year effort with the education ministry, a continental education association and an in-country technical partner to strengthen the national education database and the capacity to turn statistics into policy, launched at a Luanda event in August 2026 under a five-year, thirty-country data challenge
note: no data-quality baseline, scope, budget or completion date is published, and no contract or programme document is held

subject: dpi.mis
name: National health information system
milestone: Upgrade partnership agreed with the WHO and the University of Oslo, April 2026
position_start: DHIS2 in national use, with immunisation data rated unreliable and materially at odds with coverage surveys by a 2025 programme audit
position_end: More than 4,700 registered users on a platform a joint technical mission in March 2026 found working as a solid national platform, with agreed next steps to optimise DHIS2, harmonise data across information flows, build decision-maker dashboards, strengthen national supply-chain systems and improve interoperability with the electronic logistics management system, on a stated shift towards open-source, nationally owned solutions sustainable in crisis conditions
note: the health statistical yearbook for 2023 was built entirely from this system's administrative records and published three years after its reference year

subject: dpi.mis
name: Observa Mais satellite crop-monitoring platform
milestone: Third province installation, at an agricultural institute in Malanje
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The national space programme office installed its satellite-imagery and artificial-intelligence crop-monitoring platform at an agricultural technical institute in Malanje, the third province served after Luanda and Bengo, training one computing lecturer and 15 students as multipliers and certifying five provincial specialists; five further provinces are named for installation. A technical team was separately reported rehabilitating a connectivity point at Marimba
note: three provinces of eighteen, with the deployment measured in people trained rather than in area monitored, hectares assessed or advice issued; no imagery source, refresh cycle or cost is stated

subject: dpi.mis
name: REDISSE Phase IV regional disease-surveillance operation
milestone: Implementation completion report issued 30 November 2025
position_start: In implementation
position_end: A US$280m five-country regional disease-surveillance operation, closed by the World Bank's implementation completion report of 30 November 2025, carrying a health information and ICT subcomponent at 14% of the sector share and naming DHIS2, IDSR and EWARS among its systems; the held capture is an excerpt and states no country-specific system, coverage or outcome
note: Angola, the Central African Republic, Chad, the DRC and Congo, with ECCAS.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Vaccination registry
milestone: In use across all national vaccination campaigns
position_start: In use for real-time individual vaccination registration
position_end: Used in all national campaigns, with interoperability to the national health information system under development
note: a secretary of state's conference remarks are the only source for the current position, and no coverage or record count is published; a 2025 programme audit of 2018-2022 immunisation support rated the health ministry's management ineffective, finding immunisation data unreliable and materially at odds with coverage-survey results and administrative coverage overstated on outdated population metrics

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Count of public services available online
milestone: No service inventory published
position_end: The transition agenda counts projects, not services
note: a published service catalogue or a completion report would settle it

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital platform for public-sector internship applications
milestone: Launched at a telecommunications forum, 3 September 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The state information systems institute launched a platform centralising applications to its internship programme, removing in-person submission and issuing each applicant a tracking code and QR code; placements cover telecommunications, information technology and cybersecurity, under a partnership formalised the previous week
note: a small service, recorded because the base holds almost nothing on the state applying its own digitisation to its own processes; no placement count, application volume or programme duration is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Digital transition agenda
milestone: Project count restated at 218 on 2026-03-05
movement: No change, the project count is unstable rather than rising
position_start: 218 structuring projects at approval by Decreto Presidencial n.º 178/24 of 31 July 2024, restated as 214 in March 2025
position_end: 218 structuring projects across six strategic objectives and seven axes — citizen and business e-services, a modernised administration, interoperable technology infrastructure, security and privacy, governance and reporting, financing and sustainability, and literacy and capacity — coordinated by a modernisation institute under the presidency, with flagship projects named as the Public Administration Interoperability Platform, a single non-presential public-services window and Digital Identity
note: the founding decree already put the count at 218, so the 214 reported in March 2025 and the 218 restated in March 2026 are not a progression; nothing states how many projects are complete

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic filing of public accounts
milestone: Resolved by the Tribunal de Contas 19 June 2026
position_start: Did not exist; accounts filed on paper
position_end: The Tribunal de Contas accepts the accounts of entities under the Plano Geral de Contabilidade electronically through a Portal de Prestação de Contas inside its own integrated management system, adopted as a normative instrument by resolution rather than as the circular first proposed, covering registration and credentialing of submitting entities, training of the responsible officers, extension of filing deadlines and exceptional application to the 2025 financial year, with paper filings replaced gradually
note: no filing count or portal availability figure is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic procedure in compulsory social protection
milestone: Family benefits conditioned on electronic filing, Decreto Presidencial n.º 95/26 of 22 May 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Decreto Presidencial n.º 11/26 makes the social-security portal's domicílio electrónico the channel for filings and notifications between the managing entity and contributors, insured persons, pensioners and beneficiaries, gives electronically issued documents and acts the evidential value of paper, makes electronic availability substitute for any other form of notification, requires a digital signature on every act the managing entity issues electronically, and requires information exchange with other public and private institutions to observe national and international standards of interoperability, security and personal-data protection; Decreto Presidencial n.º 95/26 then requires reimbursement and breastfeeding-allowance claims to be filed electronically, makes the child's birth registration and vaccination card required documents, and suspends the allowance where a copy of the vaccination card is not transmitted electronically
note: a benefit decision now depends on civil-registry and health records reaching the social-security system, and no source records that exchange operating

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Health ministry external recruitment competition, online registration and marking
milestone: Complaints window opened 2026-08-25
position_start: Baseline not held
position_end: More than 420,000 registered in the 13-31 July 2026 window, of whom more than 170,000 were excluded for defective registration, leaving more than 262,000 to sit tests for 6,030 posts on 21-25 September 2026, sat simultaneously nationwide in the province of registration and marked online; candidates validate their applications on the ministry portal
note: the ministry says it has used online marking in earlier competitions; the exclusion rate is not explained beyond defective registration

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Integrated digital transformation programme for public finances
milestone: Authorised by presidential despacho as a direct award, 2026-08-17
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A programme authorised by presidential order as a direct award, covering modernisation of finance ministry services on advanced technology and a restructuring of state bodies, framed as raising revenue collection and cutting bureaucracy. Its value is not established: the earlier of the two accounts, whose reporter says he saw the presidential order, gives three different figures in one article
note: a direct award rather than a competed procurement; the supplier, scope document and delivery schedule are not published. The two press accounts are one account rather than two - the later reproduces the earlier's lead almost word for word - and the earlier is internally inconsistent on the amount, putting it at US$2.5m in the headline, US$2.4bn in the lead and more than US$2.4m in the closing line

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Mandatory electronic invoicing
milestone: 51,245 large taxpayers and state suppliers enrolled by 2026-08-23
position_start: Mandatory from 1 January 2026 for large taxpayers and state suppliers under the Regime Jurídico das Facturas (Decreto Presidencial n.º 71/25), after a penalty-free transition from 1 October to 31 December 2025 during which the tax authority certified invoicing software, with no enrolment figure published and 21 of more than 500 registered packages certified
position_end: 51,245 enrolled, 36,341,801 invoices issued
note: the enrolment and volume figures are the tax authority's own; the mandate covers large taxpayers and state suppliers, and extends to all taxpayers under the General and Simplified VAT regimes from 1 January 2027

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Public key infrastructure
milestone: Contracted inside the public digital infrastructure build
position_start: Announced in June 2025 as a ministerial intention, nothing contracted and no legal basis
position_end: Contracted as a component of the US$150m project, with the tax authority already running mandatory electronic invoicing on it in practice
note: the trust layer is being built ahead of the law that would govern it

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Tourism licensing single system
milestone: Tourist establishments moved to prior notification, 27 April 2026
position_start: Licensing on paper under the 2016 tourist-establishment regime and the 2023 restaurant regime, with a signed permit
position_end: Starting a tourist establishment needs no prior licence, authorisation or validation but a comunicação prévia filed through the Sistema Integrado de Gestão do Turismo, with the fee paid through the state's single payment reference and the notification revoked where payment does not follow; the restaurant permit's licensing-officer signature is replaced by a QR code carrying the permit's data, with prior notification of opening also routed through the same system — both measures of the Simplifica Turismo 3.0 programme
note: no count of notifications filed through the system is published

subject: digital.localgov
name: Benguela prepaid smart water meters
milestone: Installation to begin 2026-09-07
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Installation from 7 September 2026, targeting 25,000 to 26,000 meters by March 2027 on a stated budget of USD 23 million drawn from a USD 191.3 million rehabilitation and assisted-operation project across five municipalities; it starts with 500 units at Restinga in Lobito, uses 266 technicians installing meters inside homes against vandalism, and carries no cost to households
note: it follows a USD 15 million customer registration exercise that produced a 70,000-client database, replacing estimate-based billing off largely inactive analogue meters against arrears stated above 10 billion kwanzas

subject: digital.localgov
name: Integrated public security centres
milestone: Foundation stone laid in Lunda-Sul 30 July 2026
position_start: Four provinces with a centre
position_end: Cabinda inaugurated as the fifth on 9 December 2025, with a 24-hour command and video-surveillance room answering the 111 emergency number, 184 cameras carrying facial recognition, number-plate reading and protection of designated strategic state sites, and 180 staff; a sixth begun in Saurimo, Lunda-Sul, on 30 July 2026 with more than 100 cameras on the city's main arteries in a first phase and tooling for occurrence management, traffic management, city video surveillance, intelligent-camera monitoring and criminal investigation, the centres' director-general stating that expansion is under way in almost every province
note: no data-protection basis, retention rule or supervisory authority is named for the facial-recognition estate

subject: digital.localgov
name: Provincial document-management system
milestone: Approved by a provincial government 2025-12-18, implementation from January 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Integrated document and archive management for one province with a citizen application for proposals and public-tender tracking, budgeting explicitly around weak internet and power
note: the stated six-month operationalisation target passed with nothing on file either way

subject: tech.ai
name: AI supervisory or enforcement authority
status: Planned, designation left to a future regulation
milestone: Provided for but not named in the draft artificial-intelligence law, September 2025
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: No authority exists; the draft artificial-intelligence law provides for a competent authority at article 61 and leaves its designation, powers and seat to a future regulation
sources: 2025-09-01-angola-proposta-de-lei-inteligencia-artificial|2025-12-29 Review of Angola's Proposed Law on Artificial Intelligence
note: the draft repeals no existing legislation and its financial assessment is not costed

subject: tech.ai
name: Artificial-intelligence platform for the public administration
milestone: US$6 million authorised by presidential order of 27 August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The president authorised expenditure of six million United States dollars for the acquisition and implementation of an artificial-intelligence platform for the public administration, under a presidential order of 27 August 2026, and opened a public tender procedure for it
note: the order authorises money and a tender; what the platform is to do, which bodies would use it, and on what data are not stated in the announcement

subject: tech.ai
name: Digital government and public-sector AI governance framework
milestone: Consultancy tendered, March 2026
position_end: A governance framework for digital government and for artificial intelligence in the public sector put out to consultancy by the Instituto de Modernização Administrativa under the Projecto de Aceleração Digital de Angola
note: distinct from the artificial intelligence bill; nothing is published on scope, drafter or timetable beyond the terms of reference

subject: tech.ai
name: Government AI assistant
milestone: Web version launched at a trade fair 2026-07-22, replacing a text-message version
position_end: A subscription web assistant pitched at student research, offered by an operator reporting seven million clients across five provinces
note: the source confirms a prior version but does not date it; no usage figure and no model provenance

subject: tech.ai
name: Installed AI compute capacity
milestone: No figure on file
position_end: No held source states an installed accelerator capacity, AI cloud or named AI facility
note: the readiness assessment's infrastructure case rests on fibre, one satellite and data centres

subject: tech.ai
name: Tax-authority risk-analysis system
milestone: Machine-learning testing began 2024; first taxpayer notices due from June 2026
position_start: None published
position_end: In development, in-house, not in service
note: the tax authority states it builds and feeds the system in-house; no model, supplier or accuracy figure is published, and no taxpayer-facing safeguard beyond a right to be heard

subject: tech.industry
name: Incumbent operator listing
milestone: Settlement and admission to trading 2026-07-28
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: 15% of capital and votes sold for Kz 300.3bn, reported as about US$329m, at 120.72% subscription, creating 11,264 new shareholders
note: disclosure of a July cyberattack now runs under securities law rather than telecoms regulation

subject: tech.innovate
name: Incubation programme
milestone: Memorandum signed 2025-03-14
position_start: An incubation programme with institutional and technical support, physical space, training and investor introductions
position_end: Unchanged; no cohort, intake number, graduate or funding outcome published in seventeen months

subject: tech.innovate
name: Innovation ranking
milestone: Country profile published for 2025
position_end: 138th of 139 economies, worse on outputs than inputs, with no cluster in the world's top innovation clusters
sources: 2025-01-01 WIPO Global Innovation Index 2025 - Angola profile
note: a six-year trend running 132nd, 127th, 132nd, 133rd, 138th

subject: tech.innovate
name: Only mobility startup with named investors
milestone: Selected for a global accelerator cohort, April 2026
position_end: The country's only entrant in a fifteen-startup cohort drawn from about 2,600 applications, with AI-powered credit scoring to formalise motorcycle-taxi work and US$4.6m raised across named investors
sources: 2026-04-21 Meet the 15 Startups Joining the Google for Startups Accelerator Africa Class 10|2026-03-30-bfa-asset-management-kimbo-fund-angola-startups

subject: tech.innovate
name: Public-finance innovation lab
milestone: Launched 2026-03-30
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A finance-ministry innovation lab whose first proof of concept was qualified digital signatures in an internally built document system
note: no budget, headcount or project pipeline published

subject: tech.innovate
name: Startup population and funding penetration
milestone: An ecosystem assessment published November 2023
position_start: About 125 startups, with no exit event yet
position_end: Unchanged; fewer than 2% of identified startups have secured venture funding, with angel and seed structures largely absent
note: no newer count has been published, including by the ministry that sponsored the startups law

subject: capacity.literacy
name: National digital-literacy programme
milestone: No named instrument on file
position_end: The base carries digital literacy only as clauses inside other instruments, with no national programme, budget line, target or trained-population figure
note: a ministry or education programme document would settle it

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Ngola Digital school computer laboratories
milestone: Laboratory of 25 computers inaugurated at a polytechnic 2026-08-21
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: More than 2,000 computers installed across 88 schools nationwide on the minister's own count, the latest a 25-computer laboratory serving 3,051 students at a polytechnic
note: the totals are the telecommunications minister's own; no programme budget, connectivity provision or maintenance arrangement is published

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Public administration e-learning platform
milestone: Local agent training authorised 2026-08-27
position_end: a presidential order authorising the training of local agents, framed as the step that follows investment in digital infrastructure
note: the base holds no earlier position on public-administration e-learning

subject: capacity.training
name: Space-technology training and certification programme
milestone: A satellite-terminal training cohort, June 2026
position_end: More than 5,600 university students given free satellite access and more than 100 students in a Luanda cohort alongside operators and manufacturers
note: the curriculum covers terminal installation, integration, service pricing and billing

subject: capacity.training
name: Technology centre for young people
milestone: Centre entered service, August 2026
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A new technology centre entered service, framed around protecting citizens' data and training young people
note: no intake, curriculum, cost or site detail is published, and the data-protection framing is the ministry's rather than a stated function of the centre

subject: capacity.training
name: Vendor cybersecurity training commitment
milestone: Announced at a business summit 2025-06-25
position_start: US$25m of a US$170m investment earmarked for a national cybersecurity agency plus vendor academy training
position_end: Unchanged; no trainee count, cohort, curriculum or disbursement published in the fourteen months since

subject: capacity.research
name: Science and technology park
milestone: Inaugurated 2026-06-29
position_start: Provided for within the Sistema Nacional de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (Decreto Presidencial n.º 261/21 of 3 November 2021), with no managing entity and nothing built
position_end: Inaugurated under a US$100m development-bank science and technology project, intended to link academia, research, companies and young entrepreneurs; Decreto Presidencial n.º 77/26 of 24 April 2026 authorised the finance and higher-education ministers to create its managing entity as a state-owned public limited company, with the state's shareholding exercised by the public-asset institute and sector direction set by the higher-education ministry
note: no tenant, occupancy, disbursement or operating budget published

subject: capacity.research
name: Statistical capacity project
milestone: First component opened 16 September 2025
position_start: A US$60m loan, active from 2022 to 2027, supporting statistics-office modernisation, household surveys and dissemination
position_end: The first component under way: an inventory and evaluation of the administrative data already held across the public administration, and statistical products built on it, opened with Statistics Portugal and the World Bank on 16 September 2025, with Statistics Portugal offering its Infraestrutura Nacional de Dados and the Informação Empresarial Simplificada return that let it retire its own annual business survey
note: no disbursement or restructuring figure is on file; it financed the census machinery this report leans on, though no source links the two

subject: include.access
name: Accessibility law
milestone: Lei n.º 10/16, 27 July 2016
position_start: In force
position_end: In force, unamended: general norms, conditions and criteria for people with disability or reduced mobility
note: no digital-accessibility standard, audit or enforcement action under it is on record

subject: include.access
name: Bancarisation rate
milestone: Ministerial statement to a regional meeting
position_start: No official rate held; a 2023 industry figure put roughly half of the population unbanked
position_end: About 32% of the population, 5.7 million citizens, in the banking system, targeting 36% and about eight million by 2027
sources: 2026-07-09-nova-etapa-estrategia-nacional-de-inclusao-financeira|2023-06-26 Mobile Money in Angola - How Afrimoney is paving the way
note: the 2023 and 2026 figures use different bases and are not a series

subject: include.access
name: Cash-transfer programme
milestone: A single social register launched in the week ending 2026-07-25
position_start: Kwenda established by Decreto Presidencial n.º 125/20 of 4 May 2020 and financed by a US$320m World Bank loan committed in July 2019 for the transfer and for the delivery systems behind it, with more than 247,000 households reached against a 1.6 million family target
position_end: More than 1.3 million households and about 6.5 million citizens reached, with a single social register now the centralised targeting database
sources: 2026-07-25-angola-cadastro-social-unico-launch|2019-06-28 World Bank - Strengthening the National Social Protection System Project (Angola)|2020-05-04-decreto-presidencial-125-20-programa-kwenda|2019-07-16-world-bank-ago-2019-strengthening-national-social-protection-system
note: no enrolment target, data-protection basis or governing instrument stated for the register at launch

subject: include.access
name: Digital inclusion grants component
milestone: Named in the 2024 loan agreement
position_start: A component named for grants to non-governmental and community groups for community digital spaces and digital literacy, with no allocation published
position_end: Still no allocation, grantee, disbursement or beneficiary count
note: a procurement or disbursement report would settle it

subject: include.access
name: Identity-card universalisation plan
milestone: More than 4,000 cards issued in 16 days in one municipality, to 2026-08-18
position_start: Card printing centralised at a single national production centre
position_end: Printing posts in all 21 provincial capitals, two to three printers per province planned, mobile brigades in remote municipalities, and three phases covering unregistered adults, cards at birth and replacement of degraded documents; a provincial campaign issued and delivered more than 4,000 cards in 16 days in a single municipality
note: the 24-to-48-hour issuance target is reached in some localities only

subject: include.access
name: National financial inclusion strategy
milestone: Launched December 2025
position_start: Did not exist; the draft Estratégia Nacional de Inclusão Financeira 2025-2027, prepared by a central-bank-convened commission with World Bank technical support, went to public consultation on 5 December 2025 naming transactional accounts and digital payments as its first pillar and women, the rural population, farmers, informal workers, adolescents and young people as its priority segments
position_end: Financial inclusion at 51.7% in the first quarter of 2026 against a 65% target for 2027, with the next phase to let mobile and digital payment providers extend credit
note: the draft put to consultation is held; the adopted text is not, and the later figures are ministerial statements

subject: include.access
name: Public computer rooms and free internet points
milestone: New rooms and free internet points opened in Luanda and Icolo e Bengo, 2026-08-22
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: The telecommunications ministry opened further computer rooms and free public internet points in Luanda and Icolo e Bengo; no national count of sites, users or budget line is on file

subject: include.divides
name: Commercial satellite access programme
milestone: First regulator licence to a startup 2026-07-02
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A commercial access hub opened in December 2025, when the telecommunications minister presented the commercial tier of Conecta Angola running on ANGOSAT-2 and framed it as a business opening for local entrepreneurs able to resell communications services in hard-to-reach areas, with the free social tier continuing alongside it; 37 firms were in the integration process by April 2026 and a first startup was licensed to resell access
note: bandwidth, pricing and operator access terms remain undisclosed

subject: include.divides
name: Conecta Angola satellite connectivity points
milestone: Two localities connected, 27 and 28 August 2026
position_start: Not held
position_end: A national space programme project carrying internet and communication over the ANGOSAT-2 satellite to border zones and isolated communities. In the last week of August 2026 the restoration and migration of antennas reached two localities: a point recovered at Quiage commune in Bengo province, stated to serve five thousand residents, and a connection under way at Quirimbo municipality in Cuanza-Sul, delivered by startups of the national space programme and announced by the provincial registries and administrative modernisation office. No national site count, service specification, tariff, uptime record or programme budget is published
note: state news agency reports of individual site commissionings; the five-thousand figure is a beneficiary estimate for a commune rather than a connection count, and the base holds no running total of points restored or live

subject: include.divides
name: Satellite connectivity programme
milestone: 20,000 students stated by the minister 2026-07-13
position_start: 27 locations and about 366,000 citizens stated to a UN body (2025-11)
position_end: Six universities and more than 300 localities where mobile operators are absent, with 20,000 students stated, against 27 locations and about 366,000 citizens stated to a UN body in November 2025
note: the white-space leg connected 3,972 students at two schools, a different measure

subject: include.divides
name: Universal service fund
status: Implemented, no accounts or disbursement on record
milestone: Regulation gazetted 2010-11-26
position_start: On statute since 2010 and funded by 1% of telecom operators' gross revenue, with no accounts published
position_end: Unchanged; the fund and its 1% levy remain on statute, it may make non-repayable grants for non-commercial universal-service expansion but is barred from subsidising operating costs, and no accounts, grant or disbursement have been published for any year
note: required by article 15 of Lei n.º 8/01; whether 1% is still the rate in force is not established

subject: data.statistics
name: Census portal and statistics application
milestone: Launched 2026-07-02
position_start: Did not exist; census results were available only as reports
position_end: A public portal with demographic, social, economic and housing indicators by geographic level, plus a mobile application carrying macroeconomic series, built by the statistics office's own staff
note: no open-data licence, bulk download or programming interface is stated

subject: data.statistics
name: National statistical authority
milestone: New organic statute, Decreto Presidencial n.º 43/26 of 10 March 2026
position_start: Constituted under the Lei do Sistema Estatístico Nacional (Lei n.º 3/11 of 14 January 2011) and governed by the 2017 organic statute
position_end: Restated as the national statistical authority with technical, administrative, financial and patrimonial autonomy under the superintendence of the ministerial department responsible for planning, with technical independence, neutrality, impartiality, confidentiality and transparency written into the text and a reorganisation into five executive directorates plus local services; the 2017 statute is revoked
note: autonomy and independence as written in the statute; no source records the reorganisation taking effect

subject: data.statistics
name: National statistics development strategy
milestone: Approval announced as forthcoming, with a statistics-law revision to follow
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: A new strategy for the 2026 to 2032 cycle, widening the national statistical system
note: no source confirms the council session, the law revision or the promised user survey took place

subject: data.statistics
name: RGPH 2024 population and housing census
milestone: Provincial reports issued, Icolo e Bengo published 2026-02-20
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Provincial reports are being issued; the Icolo e Bengo report gives the province 1,523,457 people, 150,787 above the figure in the institute’s own summary report, and differencing the two municipal tables places the whole of that gap in one municipality, Sequele
note: The two published figures for the same province are inconsistent and the base carries no reconciliation.

subject: data.open
name: Access to administrative documents law
milestone: Enacted as Lei n.º 11/02, 16 August 2002
position_start: In force
position_end: In force, unamended
note: no implementing regulation, oversight body or request statistics is on record

subject: data.open

milestone: Committed in the digital acceleration project's safeguards plan, 23 October 2025
position_end: Component 2 of the Projecto de Aceleração Digital de Angola commits to creating a shared data-governance framework, shared infrastructure, an open-data portal and electronic services; nothing is published as operating
note: the commitment is recited in a safeguards instrument rather than in a data policy of its own

subject: data.satellite
name: Commercial access to the national satellite
milestone: Opened to commercial providers December 2025
position_start: In orbit and operated from a national control centre, government use only
position_end: A commercial provider market open, with 37 firms in the commercial arm by April 2026 and a first private licence issued in July 2026
note: no transponder capacity, pricing or revenue figure is published

subject: data.satellite

milestone: Memorandum signed with the meteorological institute and a regional science centre
position_start: Launched by the telecommunications ministry in June 2025, developed by the space agency with MIT and financed by NASA, aimed at Cunene, Huíla and Namibe
position_end: A memorandum to implement, operationalise and expand the platform, providing for sharing of satellite, climate and environmental data, development of drought-forecasting models, products, services and applications, technical training of national specialists, joint research and scientific dissemination, and integration of the platform into regional and continental networks
note: the source dates its own report but not the signing, which it places only as recent

subject: data.satellite
name: Earth-observation satellite
milestone: A system key-point milestone validated 2026-05-14
position_start: Financing signed at about EUR 225m in January 2025, with no build kicked off
position_end: Under construction after a March 2026 kick-off, with first ground infrastructure delivered from June 2026 and a design of more than 1,000 high-resolution images a day
note: no launch date is published

subject: geopol.usa
name: International wholesale partnership
milestone: Partnership agreement signed and reported 2026-05-21
position_start: Did not exist
position_end: Combines the state cable company's three subsea systems with a US network of more than 300 metro markets and 386,000 km of fibre; no value, term or capacity commitment stated

subject: geopol.usa
name: Transport corridor fibre link
milestone: The ministry states domestic subsea cable work under way 2026-03-26
position_end: A domestic submarine cable to interlink the main coastal cities, with the transport corridor connected to international systems; no route, cost, contractor, financier or completion date stated
note: the base names no US instrument, agency or financing for the corridor's digital leg

subject: geopol.usa

milestone: Announced at a business summit 2025-06-24
position_start: US$170m announced with a US$25m first phase, nothing built
position_end: Unchanged; the first phase for a national cybersecurity agency and vendor training, plus an undersea cable, with no disbursement, contract or delivery on record in fourteen months
note: nothing links this agency phase to the cyber centre created by decree six months later

subject: geopol.china
